title: Context-Aware Tool Selection Audit Harness
creator: Riley Chen
description: Build an audit/eval harness that continuously measures tool/function selection accuracy and argument validation fidelity across config and model rollouts. This harness will: 1) run a daily golden and adversarial corpus against the service under the current model/config, 2) compute per-tool precision/recall and argument-schema pass rates, 3) surface regressions tied to model/config diffs, and 4) trigger alerts or rollback hooks for threshold breaches. The goal is to detect subtle regressions introduced by kernel changes, quantization profiles, routing policy updates, or model swaps that change tool chooser behavior or argument formatting.
acceptance_criteria: Daily run that executes 5k shards of golden prompts and 1k adversarial prompts against canary and baseline endpoints
Compute and store per-tool selection metrics (precision, recall, top-3 coverage) and argument-validation rates to Console (time series + per-run histogram)
Automated diff that attributes metric deltas to specific config changes (model_id, quant_profile, routing_policy) when available
Alert integration: create PagerDuty incident if selection accuracy drops >3% absolute for high-usage tools OR argument-failure-rate increases >1% absolute
Canary gating: block rollout when golden-set emulated user flows drop below baseline by configured thresholds
Reports link back to a new Confluence doc and a GitHub PR template for rollback/actionable remediation
implementation_notes: Harness will live as a new job in evals-runner with separate runner clients for canary and baseline endpoints
Use existing schema-checker lib to validate function arguments; extend it to return structured canonicalization diffs (string-normalization, numeric-casting failures)
Metric definitions: tool_selection_precision = TP / (TP + FP); top-3 coverage = fraction where expected tool is in top-3 choices; arg_pass_rate = number of args that pass schema checks / total args
Adversarial corpus generator: seed from recent production mis-invocations + synthetic perturbations (paraphrase, missing context, truncated KV-cache states)
Storage: results written to evals-s3 bucket and indexed into console-timeseries; small runs stored as dataset artifacts (jsonl)
Attribution: correlate run metadata with deployment metadata (model sha, quant tag, runtime flags) pulled from deployment manifest for diffing

2026-02-23 - Emma Sorensen: Design review - we decided to prioritize top-1 precision and arg-pass-rate for P0 tools (payment, billing, secrets-redaction). Trade-off: top-3 coverage will be computed but not gated on rollouts initially

2026-03-01 - Infra (Jamal): Need to limit canary run qps to avoid overloading dedicated pools. Plan: shard runs across midnight UTC and cap to 250 rps per pool. Follow-up: add a circuit-breaker if error budget low
2026-03-05 - QA (Priya): Added adversarial prompt suite (format polymorphism + nested JSON args). Early runs show 0.8% arg canonicalization failures for json-typed args with quantized models

2026-03-09 - PM (Noah): Approved alert thresholds and onboarding doc. Next: wire PagerDuty and add Slack summary in #invocations-alerts channel. Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INV/Tool+Selection+Audit+Harness

2026-03-12 - Emma Sorensen: Implementation in progress. Backend job scaffolding complete; writing results to evals-s3 works. Next sprint: integrate attribution so run reports include model/config diff metadata. Planned follow-ups include a runbook and PR template for rollbacks
notes_summary: Scope: starting with tool selection and argument validation only (no reranking or downstream tool execution correctness).
Longer-term: include per-tool output-quality evals (semantic fidelity) and tie scoring to Optimize suggestions
Privacy: runs must redact PII and honor customer opt-outs; use scrubber from prod-ingest
